summary: Monica Esposito worked in sinology and religious studies. She earned a PhD at Paris Diderot University and completed postdoctoral studies at Ca' Foscari, Paris, and Kansai Universities before serving as an associate professor at Kyoto University in 2003.

Monica L. Smith is a scholar of archaeology and Indology who studied at the University of Michigan (circa 1992–1997). She held a post at the University of Pittsburgh (2000–2002) before becoming a professor at UCLA in 2002.

Monier Monier-Williams was an Indologist and linguist who studied under Horace Hayman Wilson at Oxford. He taught at East India Company College and Cheltenham College before serving as Boden Professor of Sanskrit at Oxford from 1860 to 1887.

Monika Boehm-Tettelbach is an Indologist who studied under Heinz-Jürgen Pinnow at the Free University of Berlin and completed her habilitation at Bonn. She held professorships at the Universities of Cologne, Bamberg, and Heidelberg (1990–2006).
Monika Nowakowska is a scholar in Indology and philosophy who has held posts at the University of Warsaw (attested 2010 and 2026).

Monika Zin works in Indology, Buddhist studies, and archaeology. She studied at Jagiellonian University, the Academy of Fine Arts Vienna, and the University of Munich, where she taught (circa 1994–2015), later leading research projects in Leipzig.
Moodeen Sheriff was an Indologist and medical professional who studied at Madras Medical College and served as Native Surgeon at the Triplicane Dispensary from 1858 to 1889.

Moriichi Yamazaki is an Indologist and Buddhist studies scholar who studied at Tohoku University and Cambridge under K. R. Norman. He taught at Sendai College and served as president of Hosen Gakuen College and Kodomo Kyoiku Hosen College.

Moritz Abraham Stern was a mathematician and linguist who studied under Carl Friedrich Gauss and Karl Otfried Müller at Göttingen. He served as an extraordinarius professor at the University of Göttingen from 1829 to 1884.

Moriya Okano is a scholar of Buddhist studies and religious studies who studied at Kanto Gakuin University. He has held positions at Musashino University and the Samgraha Institute for Psychological and Spiritual Studies (attested 2002).

Moriz Haupt was a German linguist who studied under Gottfried Hermann at Leipzig University. He served as a professor at Leipzig (1843–1851) and Humboldt University of Berlin (1853), and as perpetual secretary of the Prussian Academy of Sciences.

Moriz Winternitz was an Indologist and Buddhist scholar who studied at Vienna under Georg Bühler and Friedrich Max Müller. He taught at the Association for Women in Oxford, Visva-Bharati University, and the German University of Prague (circa 1902–1934).

Morten Schlütter is a Buddhist studies and sinology scholar who earned his PhD from Yale under Stanley Weinstein. He taught at Yale, Komazawa, Victoria, UCLA, and Wisconsin–Madison, and became an associate professor at the University of Iowa.

Mortimer Wheeler was an archaeologist and Indologist educated at UCL. He directed the National Museum Cardiff and the London Museum, founded the UCL Institute of Archaeology, and served as Director-General of the Archaeological Survey of India (1944–1948).
Morton Klass was a scholar of religion and Indology who studied at Columbia University under Conrad M. Arensberg. He taught at Bennington College, Barnard College, and Columbia University.

Motohiro Yoritomi was a scholar of Buddhist studies and Indology who studied at Kyoto University under Gadjin M. Nagao and Yuichi Kajiyama. He was a professor at Shuchiin University and the Graduate University for Advanced Studies.

Motoi Ono is a scholar of Buddhist studies, Indology, and philosophy. He studied under Yasunori Ejima, attended the University of Tsukuba and the University of Vienna, and served as an associate professor at Tsukuba (circa 2004).

Mou Zongsan was a philosopher and sinologist who studied at Peking University under Shili Xiong. He held posts at National Taiwan University, National Taiwan Normal University, Tunghai University, the University of Hong Kong, and New Asia College.
Moumita Hossain is a history and archaeology researcher who studied under Ranjit Sen and serves as a research fellow at the Asiatic Society (attested 2026).

Mrinal Kanti Gangopadhyay is an Indology and philosophy scholar. He served as a professor at Vidyasagar College (attested 1970–1975, 1990) and lectured in Sanskrit at the University of Calcutta (attested 1982, 1994).
